name: jcouball
description: James Couball's agent plugins: cross-repo skills and commands for writing, explaining, and maintaining Ruby open source projects.

plugins.name: jcouball-writing
plugins.description: Writing and explanation tools. Strips AI tells from prose while keeping reference docs dry, and explains technical subjects in plain language without dropping the real terms.

plugins.name: jcouball-github
plugins.description: GitHub pull request workflow tools. Resolves PR review feedback and suppressed Copilot comments, folds fixes into the commits that introduced them, requests fresh Copilot reviews, and rebases a branch onto the default branch without opening an editor. Audits repository settings and agent guidance against a guardrails baseline.

plugins.name: jcouball-marketplace
plugins.description: Commands for maintaining the jcouball marketplace: promote a project skill into it, add a project-local override file, scaffold a new skill with the overrides contract, and vendor or update third-party skills.

plugins.name: jcouball-testing
plugins.description: Testing vocabulary and standards. A guide that defines the terms for talking about tests, classifies them on six dimensions, and says how to choose which kind to write, with sections mapping it to Ruby, RSpec, and Rails.

plugins.name: jcouball-worktrees
plugins.description: Worktree placement. A WorktreeCreate hook puts the worktrees Claude Code makes in a .worktrees directory beside the repository's main worktree rather than in .claude/worktrees inside it, so a repository's linters and file walkers never descend into another branch's files. A WorktreeRemove hook takes them away again.
